newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak depo rates seen lower, mkt eyeing c.bank.
newsitem.headline: Slovak depo rates seen lower, mkt eyeing c.bank.

text.p: Slovak short-term interbank money market rates, contrary to market expectations, rose in heavier trade on Friday, but dealers said they remained bearish for the near-term.
Slovak interbank money rates up to two weeks rose one full percentage point in early activity, steadying at Thursday's level of about 21 percent offer.
They said a decline in rates may start as early as Friday afternoon due to a recent inflow of foreign funds, eventually falling to the central bank's repo rate of about 17 percent.

They added the market was closely watching the central bank for a reverse repo rate cut or some administrative measures after Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's statement earlier this week on measures being taken to lower rates.

"Regardless of the expected measures, which will certainly be taken, banks will be filled significantly with funds next week from new inflows, driving prices down to 17-18 percent, not lower," Jaroslav Hora, chief-dealer at VUB Bank, said.
"The market is very cautious...thus even larger banks set deposit rates higher to be more attractive (than this morning's NBS) tender," he added.
But Martin Hrozany, chief-dealer at Slovenska Sporitelna, said the increase was "surprising".

"Market liquidity is sufficient, though thanks to hot money, and rates will fall slightly for the time being. But as long as liquidity is drained for 17 percent, rates will not dip below this level," he said.
Dealers said they estimated that the rates have attracted at least some $150 million in foreign funds, which had been deposited mainly for one month over the past week.
"The NBS still stands by its attitude (to drain liquidity), but it is no longer willing to pay what banks demand for it -- this is a change," Hora said.
